fix.title: Resolve: {0}
fix.rdpEnabledWhat: turn on Remote Desktop on this PC.
fix.rdpEnabledWhy: it is what opens the apps on the other computer.
fix.rdpEnabledEffect: accounts of this PC that have a password can sign in through the network (always with Network Level Authentication).
fix.rdpPolicyWhat: set the Windows policy that turns Remote Desktop off to "allow".
fix.rdpPolicyWhy: while the policy blocks it, Remote Desktop stays off even when turned on in Settings.
fix.rdpPolicyEffect: if the policy comes from your company (domain), it may come back.
fix.rdpServiceWhat: set the Remote Desktop service (TermService) to Manual start and start it.
fix.rdpServiceWhy: without the service this PC does not accept connections.
fix.firewallWhat: enable the Windows Firewall rules for Remote Desktop (port 3389).
fix.firewallWhy: the firewall is blocking connections from other computers.
fix.firewallEffect: port 3389 opens to the network; only someone with a user name and password of this PC gets in.
fix.networkWhy: on a Public network Windows blocks connections coming from other computers, including WRApperture's.
fix.networkEffect: other computers on this network can see this PC (network discovery and sharing). Only do it on trusted networks, such as home or office.
fix.remoteUsersWhat: add the account {0} to the Remote Desktop Users group.
fix.remoteUsersWhy: standard users can only sign in remotely when they are in that group.
fix.remoteUsersEffect: this account can sign in to this PC remotely with its password.
fix.passwordlessWhat: turn off "For improved security, only allow Windows Hello sign-in for Microsoft accounts".
fix.passwordlessWhy: with it on, the Microsoft account cannot sign in with a password, and Remote Desktop requires the password.
fix.passwordlessEffect: you keep signing in here with PIN or biometrics; the password is accepted too. Afterwards, sign in to this PC once with the Microsoft account password.
